body: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to support consequential decisions, yet their reliability under equivalent representations of uncertainty remains unclear. Existing work has documented prompt sensitivity, cognitive biases, and confidence miscalibration, but it is still unknown whether high-stakes advice changes when the same probability is expressed through complementary gain and loss frames. We introduce FrameBench-HPS, a controlled benchmark of 2,880 prompts derived from 240 high-stakes scenarios across healthcare, finance, education/career, and legal/consumer-rights domains. Across seven LLMs, gain-loss framing changes the recommendation category in 32.4% of complete groups, with most changes involving uncertainty rather than direct reversals. Human evaluation confirms corresponding shifts in perceived risk and directiveness. Robustness experiments show that framing effects persist under conversational paraphrases and exceed ordinary repeated-generation variability. Probability canonicalization substantially reduces framing sensitivity, identifying probability representation as a practical target for improving consistency in high-stakes LLM decision support.
summaryZh: 相同的概率，不同的建议：高风险 LLM 决策支持中的得失框架效应。大型语言模型 (LLM) 越来越多地用于支持相应的决策，但它们在等效不确定性表示下的可靠性仍不清楚。现有的工作已经记录了即时敏感性、认知偏差和信心校准错误，但仍不清楚当通过互补的收益和损失框架表达相同的概率时，高风险建议是否会改变。
